conventions.convention: Rounds run from 1 through a positive finite horizon T. Choices use earlier revealed history and learner-private randomness; current loss is not observed before choosing. Random choices are measurable in their declared target measurable spaces.

Full information reveals the entire loss function after choosing; bandit feedback reveals only the played loss. Oblivious, non-anticipating adaptive, and current-choice-reactive adversaries have distinct timing.

Stochastic arms have fixed Borel reward laws with finite first absolute moments. The fixed-law and conditional-mean identities hold on every measurable pre-reward history-and-arm event contained in the selected-arm event.

Every minimum used in regret is assumed finite and attained. Expected regret requires a measurable, integrable regret random variable. Pseudo-regret uses mean gaps; realized reward regret uses μ* minus the observed reward.

Comparator path length is 1 plus the sum of successive norm distances. Intervals are nonempty contiguous integer intervals; adaptive regret is their maximum interval regret. Strong adaptivity is relative to a specified model and base static-regret bound.

load_bearing.statement: The learner chooses from a nonempty action set using earlier revealed history and available private randomness, before observing the current loss, and receives feedback after incurring that loss; randomized choices are measurable.

The stochastic finite-arm reward model specifies fixed integrable arm laws and explicitly assumes the eventwise conditional-mean identity E[1_B Y_t] = μ_i P(B) for pre-reward history-and-arm events B contained in {A_t=i}; adversarial timing and feedback classes are distinguished.

Static regret subtracts the finite attained minimum cumulative loss of one fixed comparator; dynamic regret subtracts a supplied comparator sequence's cumulative loss; interval regret uses one fixed comparator on that interval. Stochastic pseudo-regret sums mean gaps, while realized reward regret sums μ* minus observed rewards.

For integers T,N≥1, measurable finite-arm choices A_t, integrable rewards Y_t, and finite means satisfying E[Y_t 1_{A_t=i}] = μ_i P(A_t=i), set μ*=max_i μ_i and N_i(T)=sum_t 1_{A_t=i}. Then E[R_T^rew] = E[bar R_T] = sum_i (μ*−μ_i) E[N_i(T)].

published_dependencies.used_for: Probability spaces, measurable events, and arm laws of total mass one.
Measurable action choices and Borel-measurable real rewards.
Expected regret and arm means as Lebesgue integrals, with integrability qualifications.
Finite linearity of expectation in the regret decomposition and stochastic example.
Converting expected arm indicators to selection probabilities and expected pull counts.

seams_checked.note: Checked the page requirement and algorithm/theorem interfaces against the supplier definitions. Hedge preserves full-information timing and its fixed loss-sequence assumption for expected static regret. OGD states comparator-wise bounds and invokes static regret only when the minimum is finite and attained.

The reward-stack definition preserves non-anticipating choices, finite first moments, and both regret conventions. Its conditional-law lemma supplies the eventwise mean identity before explore-then-commit and UCB invoke the gap-weighted expected-count decomposition.

The page requirement resolves to the generic timing definition. The contextual model explicitly adds current context and available features as pre-action side information, requires measurable selected features, and observes reward noise afterward; it identifies this extension explicitly rather than attributing current-context availability to the generic supplier.
